$comment: PROJECT-MANIFEST BUILD with a preBuildScripts hook that GENERATES the source it then compiles. This is the corpus's runtime witness for the whole chain -- script spawn -> file written -> sources glob expanded -> compile -> link -> spawn -> exit code -- and every link in it is load-bearing: `sources` names NO file that exists in git, only the pattern `generated_*.c`, and Program::compileProject treats a zero-match pattern as a hard D_FileNotFound rather than an empty build. So a hook that does not run, runs in the wrong directory, or writes the wrong name cannot produce a green run. A hook that merely TOUCHED a file would prove none of that.
$commentPlatformArms: Two arms over the closed windows/linux/darwin runOn vocabulary, producing byte-identical C. windows spawns `powershell -File gen_answer_source.ps1`; linux and darwin spawn `/bin/sh gen_answer_source.sh`. Both interpreters are argv[0] and are spawned DIRECTLY -- there is no shell in between -- so the script file travels as an ARGUMENT and needs no executable bit, which is what lets it survive the corpus runners' fs::copy_file mirroring. Each script file states its own PATH assumption for its leg.
$commentArtifactRouting: artifactName pins the binary's base name so it does not follow the generated source's stem. Program::compileProject forces setPerFormatOutputSubdir(true), so each target's artifact lands at <output>/<formatName>/prebuild_codegen<ext> -- which is why the expected.json target entries are read with a per-format subdirectory by both runners.
